briefConventions: This repo is PUBLIC and open-sourceable — never commit engagement specifics, client names, real figures from a live plan, or anything identifying a subject. Worked examples in the skills must be generic. State (vaults, outputs) lives OUTSIDE the skill, under ~/Documents/go-to-market/<slug>/; the repo holds method and tools only, never user data. The shipped/repo split is a directory: everything under bin/ ships to users as two implementations held byte-identical by a JSON parity gate — bin/vault-lint.sh (POSIX /bin/sh, no bashisms) and bin/vault-lint.ps1 (Windows PowerShell 5.1) — and a session invokes whichever one matches the shell tool it actually has: Claude Code puts an enabled plugin's bin/ on that tool's PATH, so skills invoke it bare as 'vault-lint.sh' or 'vault-lint.ps1', never by path, and a runtime prerequisite discovered at the moment of use is a broken product. Everything under scripts/ (check.mjs, fixtures/, parity/) is contributor-only, never loaded and never on a user's PATH, and may assume Node. Both bin/ implementations are ZERO-dependency (no package.json, no lockfile, no install step) on supply-chain grounds: a tool that reads a user's private business corpus should not carry a transitive dependency tree. Prose style: section headings are action titles stating the finding, not labels; banned words are revolutionary, disruptive, game-changing, cutting-edge, delve, tapestry, paramount, seamless-as-filler, landscape-as-filler. Every rule added to a skill must name the failure it prevents — a rule with no failure mode behind it is ceremony and gets cut. Run 'node scripts/check.mjs' green before opening a PR, plus 'sh scripts/fixtures/run-fixtures.sh' and 'node scripts/parity/parity.mjs' if you touched bin/vault-lint.sh or bin/vault-lint.ps1 — the fixtures suite proves each script still does what it claims, the parity gate proves the two scripts still agree with each other, and each catches a failure the other can't. gate and scopedCheck are the same command and there is no queue — run it yourself, then open a DRAFT PR into the integration branch: the draft PR is your hand-back, and only the reviewer flips it ready (gh pr ready) before merging, because GitHub refuses to merge a draft and that is the interlock against merging an unread diff. Assume your change ships and needs the version in .claude-plugin/plugin.json moved forward plus a matching '## <version>' heading in CHANGELOG.md: an install is pinned to that string, so merging under an unchanged version ships nothing. Only scripts/, .github/, .agents/, AGENTS.md, CHANGELOG.md, docs/ and .gitignore are exempt (the exempt regex in .github/workflows/ci.yml is authoritative — change both together). Read AGENTS.md before changing anything. Never rebase, never self-merge. Merge commits, not squash.
